4.5 Mobile Architectural Considerations and Overview 
The mobile applications architecture is designed around the Model-View-
ViewModel pattern. This approach enables a separation of concerns by 
segmenting the application into three distinct components, facilitating a modular 
approach to the applications development (Chugh, 2022). 
Model: Within the applications architecture, the models are responsible for 
storing and managing application data, and abstracting any data related 
complexities. This comes with the additional benefit of ensuring these classes 
are easily testable. 
View: For the application, the views are designed with the sole responsibility of 
presenting the data given by the ViewModel. The view should adapt its content 
based on changes to the model.  
ViewModel: The ViewModel will act as a controller, managing presentation, logic, 
and state. Critically it will transform any content from the model, into a human 
readable format for the view. Here the developer decided to diverge from this 
pattern slightly by asynchronously fetching data from the cloud, which would 
typically be the responsibility of the model; this decision was driven by the 
pragmatic benefits of streamlining loading screens and general smoother 
operations. 
To support the cloud-based functionalities, for content delivery and user 
authentication, the AWS Software Development Kit (SDK) will be utilised. 
Utilising S3, for retrieving educational content, including videos and documents; 
the AWS SDK enables generation of video streaming URLs, and the recursive 
scans for retrieving all lessons.
